title: What Is A Weak Chin?
author: carteremily
excerpt: If you have a less prominent chin, also known as a weak chin or jaw, it means that you have a chin that lacks definition and does not sit in proportion with your other facial features.
content:
If you have a less prominent chin, also known as a weak chin or jaw, it means that you have a chin that lacks definition and does not sit in proportion with your other facial features. You may have more of a soft chin or a receding chin. This is where the chin curves inwards towards the neck. Or maybe you have started to notice a recessed chin due to the natural ageing process. Having a weak chin is not generally a health concern and should not affect how you live your life. However, because the chin and jawline play an important role in how we look, we find more people want to fix a weak chin so that they can have more structure and definition to their lower face. If you are considering weak chin treatment, you may be surprised to know that chin surgery or chin augmentation is not your only option. In fact, one of the best ways to correct a weak chin is with the help of dermal fillers. Our aesthetic doctors at The One Clinic break down what a weak chin is and how you can achieve more structure to your chin and jaw with dermal filler treatment.

What is a weak chin or a receding chin?

In short, if you have a weak or recessed chin, your chin does not sit symmetrically with your jawline. Your chin bone may not have a prominent position on your lower face and may appear to slope back towards the neck. For many people, a weak chin is the result of a medical condition known as mandibular retrognathia or a receding chin. This is a condition whereby the lower jaw bone sits inwards. It can also lead to the upper and lower jaw not meeting together when your jaw is clenched. Your genetics can also result in you having a weak chin. If your parents have a small chin or weak upper and lower jawline, you are more likely to develop this, too.

Main causes of a weak chin

The lower and upper jaw

A weak chin can be influenced by the position of your lower and upper jawbone because of:
  • The lower jaw or mandible is underdeveloped or sits further back. This can lead to the chin looking more recessed.
  • The upper jaw can be overdeveloped. This is less common, but it can make the lower jaw and chin look weak and like it is receding.

Genetics

As we mentioned earlier, a family history of weak chins plays the biggest role in you developing a weak chin. This includes an underdeveloped jawbone, which is often a family trait.

Ageing

Ageing is a completely natural process. But as part of this process, we start to lose skin elasticity, which means we begin to see less volume and structure in our skin, causing it to sag. This is because, as we age, we begin to lose levels of collagen and elastin in the skin. These are two proteins that are crucial to giving our skin its firmness and structure. This is why we see sagging skin under the chin (double chin) and jawline (jowls).

An overbite

An overbite is when your front top teeth overlap your bottom teeth. As a result, this can push the position of your chin and lower jaw back. This leads to your chin looking weaker.

Overactive Muscles

You can also develop a weak chin if you overuse the mentalis muscle. This is the muscle that raises the skin on the chin and provides support to the lower lip. If you use this muscle too much it can result in the chin being drawn back and dimples on the chin.

Best weak chin treatment – dermal fillers

At one time, weak chin surgery and jaw surgery were the go-to options to correct a weak chin. The surgery would require the use of chin implants and jaw implants to change your facial structure and give you a more defined chin and jaw. Not only is this option costly, but it can be painful and require a lot of downtime. Today, non-surgical treatments such as chin fillers can help to fix a weak chin or weak jawline without changing your facial structure. They also require little to no downtime and can help you achieve a natural and more symmetrical lower face.

What are dermal fillers for the chin area?

Dermal filler treatment or chin filler helps to add volume and definition to the lower face to bring it in proportion with your other facial features. They are an injectable treatment that consists of hyaluronic acid as their main ingredient. This helps to boost hydration and give your skin a natural glow and youthful look. Dermal filler injections not only plump sagging skin or hollow areas around the chin and jawline, but they also smooth out lines and wrinkles. This includes chin dimples and nose-to-mouth wrinkles. At The One Clinic, our experts also use dermal fillers for other areas of the face including the cheeks, nose, lips (lip filler) and under-eye area (tear troughs).

How do chin fillers work?

At The One Clinic, we provide every patient with an in-depth consultation so that we can assess your chin shape and structure. You will meet with one of our aesthetic doctors who will look at your medical history and ask questions about your chin concerns. From this, we can build a bespoke treatment plan to correct your weak chin. If dermal fillers are right for you, we will walk you through where the injection sites will be to help create a more sculpted and defined chin area. If you will benefit from jawline fillers as well, your doctor will discuss this option with you. The doctor will inject the chin fillers using a very fine needle. This ensures the filler placement is more precise so that we can reduce any bruising you may see after treatment. Before we inject the dermal filler, we will apply a numbing cream to the chin area. This will ensure your treatment is more comfortable. Your chin filler treatment should take 30-60 minutes to complete. This will depend on what look you are hoping to achieve and if we include jawline fillers as part of your treatment plan.

How long do the results of chin fillers last?

The good news is that you will see a viable improvement in chin projection and chin shape straight away. This will continue to improve as the fillers settle, which can take up to two weeks. The results of your chin filler treatment can last for 6-18 months. This will depend on different factors such as your age, health and metabolism. We usually advise that you come back into the clinic for a top-up treatment at around the 12-month mark. This ensures that you maintain your great results.

Are chin fillers safe?

Chin fillers are a safer option than surgery for anyone looking for a more pronounced chin. They do not require opening the skin or changing your bone or face structure. Having said this, you do need to consult with a qualified doctor or nurse practitioner. This is because dermal filler treatment requires an advanced knowledge of facial anatomy. Our team of doctors at The One Clinic have over 45 years of experience between them. They understand how to inject dermal fillers at the right depth and points in the face to achieve a natural look. It is normal to see some slight swelling and bruising in the treatment area. This will go down within the first 48 hours. Your doctor will provide you with aftercare instructions to ensure you help your fillers settle and get the most out of your results.

Talk to us about weak chin treatment

If you are not sure what treatment is right for you in helping you fix your weak chin, your first step should be to talk with one of our doctors. They can help you understand why you might have a recessed chin and what treatment option will provide you with optimal results. This starts with a consultation where you can find out more about chin fillers and see what results we have helped other patients achieve. It is also your chance to get to know us more and ask any questions you might have about dermal filler treatment for the chin.

title: What Is Endolift?
author: carteremily
excerpt: In the beauty and aesthetics industry, we are always looking for the next best solution for turning back the hands of time.
content:
In the beauty and aesthetics industry, we are always looking for the next best solution for turning back the hands of time. This is where Endolift comes in. It is a revolutionary laser skin-tightening treatment that has everyone talking.  Endolift treatment is the go-to alternative for a surgical facelift. It uses laser technology to target sagging skin and stubborn fat cells, while also working to improve skin laxity. By stimulating collagen production in the skin, this treatment lifts, firms and tightens the skin.  Whether you are looking to tighten loose skin across your jawline, lift your cheeks or smooth and refine your neck area, Endolift treatment can help you see amazing results.  If you are ready to hear more about what Endolift is, how it works and its benefits, continue reading on. If you want to hear about how our doctor can help give you a sculpted appearance with Endolift, contact us via the form below.  GET IN TOUCH

What is Endolift treatment? Your alternative to a surgical facelift

If you are looking for a solution to loose skin, excess fat cells and moderate skin laxity, Endolift treatment could be the answer.  It is a minimally invasive procedure that uses laser energy to directly target the most common signs of the natural ageing process. This includes sagging skin and lines and wrinkles. It helps by sculpting the face and bringing more health and vibrancy back to the skin.  But the Endolift laser treatment does not stop there. It is also one of the latest fat reduction or body contouring treatments on the market. This is because the laser energy also targets excess fat cells, including facial fat and body fat to melt it away.  It can do this because it works in the deeper layers of the skin to kick-start collagen production. This is a natural protein in our body that gives our skin its strength and structure. As we age, we lose levels of collagen in our skin, which is why skin starts to sag. Because Endolift increases collagen in the skin, it results in skin that looks more firm and radiant. 

Endolift – key treatment areas

We know ageing affects more than just the face; it impacts different areas of the body too. This is where we use Endolift as our treatment of choice to tackle skin sagging and stubborn fat cells on the following areas of the face and body:
  • Chin and jawline 
  • Nasolabial folds
  • Smile lines and laughter lines
  • Lower eyelids (reduce skin laxity)
  • Neck and décolletage (reduce turkey neck)
  • Stomach
  • Arms
  • Inner thighs
  • Ankles
  • Knees
  • Buttock area

How can I benefit from Endolift treatment?

If you are still on the fence about Endolift laser technology, here is a breakdown of some of the reasons why patients rave about this treatment:

1. Permanently eliminate fat cells 

This fat reduction treatment melts stubborn areas of fat that are hard to lose through diet and exercise such as jowls and double chin.

2. Great for promoting skin tightening 

Through the heat of the laser energy which results in the contraction of existing collagen fibres and causes an immediate tightening of the skin.

3. Improves skin texture 

On top of tightening the skin it also helps to smooth the skin and reduce crepey skin and lines and wrinkles

4. Full rejuvenation of the skin 

As it targets both the surface of the skin and the deeper layers. 

5. No need for incisions or downtime 

This treatment works on all skin types and we can tailor it to your skin’s needs. This means there is no need to have surgery where you need to take time off to recover.

What to expect during Endolift treatment 

You will have your Endolift treatment with one of our trained doctors in our Leicester clinic. During the treatment, we use a hand-held device that has a laser fibre. This is as thin as hair, which we insert under the skin.  Most patients describe feeling comfortable throughout the procedure. However, we do use a local anaesthetic to ensure your treatment is as comfortable as possible.  Once the laser fibre is underneath the skin, the laser-induced selective heat targets the fat and melts it. This also results in the skin retracting, which reduces sagging skin and loose skin. It is because of the high-powered nature of the laser that skin tightening occurs.  The length of your treatment session will depend on which areas you are targeting. For one area of the face, it may only take ten minutes. Whereas the entire face can take up to one hour. 

Skin tightening results with Endolift laser treatment 

The results of Endolift can be different for everyone. This is because it will depend on factors such as your age, skin condition and lifestyle.  To get the best results, you will need 1-2 Endolift treatment sessions. The exact number will be discussed during your consultation so that our doctor can tailor the treatment to your specific skin goals.  You will start to see some visible improvement in the texture and firmness of your skin around 4-8 weeks after your treatment. This is so new collagen can form. Your skin will also continue to improve over the weeks and months after your final treatment. The final result is generally seen at around the 6-9 month mark.  The results of Endolift are long-lasting. Many of our patients achieve results that last for 1-2 years. This, of course, will depend on your following a good skincare routine that focuses on anti-ageing. 

Are you ready to chat about Endolift treatment?

Now that you have a good idea of what Endolift treatment is and how it can work for you, it’s time to get in touch with our team to book a consultation.  This is your opportunity to meet with a doctor, see how the treatment works in person and ask any questions you might have. It also enables our doctors to build a plan of what your skin needs and create a bespoke treatment plan to help you achieve this.  BOOK YOUR APPOINTMENT

title: Look 10 Years Younger Leicester
author: carteremily
excerpt: While ageing is a completely natural process, most of us would like to stay looking younger for longer.
content:
While ageing is a completely natural process, most of us would like to stay looking younger for longer. But how can you turn back the hands of time and look 10 years younger? The good news is that you don’t have to turn to surgical procedures to get that fresh-faced look. At The One Clinic, we can help you take ten years off your age (not literally, but aesthetically) with the help of non-surgical treatments or tweakments that help provide subtle enhancements to your skin and facial features.  We use anti-wrinkle injections and dermal fillers to visibly reduce lines, wrinkles, and sagging skin. With a course of treatment, you can achieve a more refreshed and youthful glow to your skin.  Learn more about how we use these treatments to create natural-looking results, or get in touch with our Leicester skin clinic to book a consultation with one of our cosmetic doctors.  GET IN TOUCH

How dermal fillers and anti-wrinkle injections can help your skin look ten years younger 

Dermal fillers vs anti-wrinkle treatment

There is the common misconception that anti-wrinkle treatment and dermal filler treatment do the exact same thing. While they are both treatments that target the visible signs of ageing, what they do and the results they achieve are very different.  Anti-wrinkle treatment, also known as Botox, uses botulinum toxin type A, which is a protein that blocks the signals between the nerves and facial muscles. This causes the muscles to stop contracting for a few months. The result – Botox treatment helps to smooth away the fine lines and wrinkles that form when you smile, laugh or frown. These wrinkles are known as dynamic wrinkles.  Dermal fillers, on the other hand, are an injectable treatment that uses a gel-like substance to add volume and plump the skin. Dermal filler treatment can help to restore lost volume while also adding definition and shape to different areas of the face such as the cheeks, chin and jawline.  Another benefit of dermal fillers is that they boost hyaluronic acid and collagen in the skin. These are two natural substances in the body that we lose with age but that are vital to keeping the skin strong, flexible and looking healthy. While anti-wrinkle treatment targets dynamic wrinkles, dermal fillers target the static wrinkles that remain on the face even after you stop using your muscles. Fillers help plump and fill these deep lines and wrinkles to give you a smooth and even appearance.  It is possible to combine these treatments, but you may have to have them separately to allow for both to do their job and give you the best results. 

The best areas to have Botox treatment

The most common areas to have anti-wrinkle treatment include:
  •     Frown lines – on the forehead and just above the eyebrows
  •     Forehead lines – horizontal lines across the forehead 
  •     Crow’s feet – the outer corners of the eyes (laughter lines)
  •     Bunny lines – fine lines on the sides of your nose
  •     Lip lines – from pursing or pouting your lips
 You can also use Botox treatment to reduce neck bands or neck lines, which are the horizontal lines that form due to ageing and the constant muscle movements in your neck. Another popular treatment is masseter Botox treatment, which is where we inject Botox into the masseter muscle (the muscle that connects the lower jaw to the outer lower cheek area). Doing this relaxes this muscle and can help you achieve a slimmer or more contoured jawline. 

The best areas for dermal filler treatments 

Dermal fillers can treat more areas of the face and can support the results of anti-wrinkle treatment by adding volume, shape and definition to the face.  Our cosmetic doctors use dermal filler injections to treat the following areas:
  • Lip fillers – to give more shapely and plump lip
  • Nose fillers – or non-surgical rhinoplasty to smooth a dorsal bump or create a shapely nasal tip
  • Tear trough fillers – or under-eye fillers to reduce dark circles or fill sunken tear troughs
  • Cheek fillers – to add shape and definition to the cheek area
  • Chin filler and jawline filler – often used together to fix a weak chin and jawline, while also helping to lift sagging skin or sagging jowls
  • Nasolabial folds – smoothing the lines that appear from the bottom of the nose to the top of the mouth
  • Marionette lines – reduce lines that form from the bottom of the mouth down to the chin
  • Laughter lines – also known as smile lines
  • Deep forehead lines – that sit on the skin permanently

Which lasts longer – dermal fillers or Botox?

Botox results

It takes up to two weeks for the anti-wrinkle injections to relax the facial muscles. This is when you will see your final results and fewer lines and wrinkles.  Your results should last for 3-4 months. For some people, this can be longer. At this point, your muscles will return to their normal function, and the lines and wrinkles will start to reappear.  At the three-month mark, we recommend that you book a top-up appointment to ensure you maintain your results. 

Dermal filler results

Straight after your dermal filler treatment, you will see some visible improvements in the plumpness and stricture of your skin. This will continue to improve over the next two weeks as the fillers settle into place. This is when you will see your final results.  Dermal fillers last longer than Botox. Most patients see the results of their dermal fillers for 9-12 months. This will depend on how your body responds to the fillers, your lifestyle and how quickly your body breaks them down. We recommend that you come back to the clinic at the 9-12 month mark to have a top-up treatment. This will ensure your skin stays looking smooth, plump and rejuvenated. 

How to address the other common signs of ageing

Skin pigmentation issues 

Age spots, sun spots or an uneven skin tone can also make your skin look older than you are. While skincare products such as vitamin C or retinol can go a long way to reducing, treatments such as Laser IPL, chemical peels and vampire facials can help reverse some of the damage on your skin. 

Loose skin on your chest and neck

The skin on your neck and upper chest (decolletage) can often show the visible signs of ageing such as lines, wrinkles and sagging skin. We often focus on the skin on our face, but this area is always very susceptible to ageing and environmental stress. To help lift, firm and rejuvenate loose skin, we provide Endolift treatment and Morpheus8. Both of these treatments help kick-start the production of collagen and elastin in the skin, which increases its stretch and flexibility. 

Scars and redness or rosacea

If you suffer from acne scars, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation or facial redness, this can make your skin look older and tired. To help treat this, you need to give your skin a boost of hydration and collagen to promote the growth of new and healthy skin cells.  The best treatments for these skin conditions include laser IPL, HydraFacial, chemical peels and Morpheus8.  

Talk to us about our skin treatments

To find the right treatments to help you look and feel 10 years younger, we first need to understand what skin concerns you have and what are causing the visible signs of ageing to show. This way, we can treat the issue at its source. This all starts with an initial consultation with one of our doctors at our Leicester clinic. We will assess your skin condition and talk you through the different anti-ageing treatments we offer. From this, we will develop a bespoke treatment plan that will address your concerns and help you achieve a more youthful appearance.  BOOK YOUR APPOINTMENT

title: What Is A HydraFacial?

excerpt: Everyone wants a natural glow to their skin and a more radiant complexion.
content:
Everyone wants a natural glow to their skin and a more radiant complexion. But with so many skincare products out there, it can be a challenge to figure out which ones work and which ones are best for your skin type.  What if you could find one facial treatment that tackles your specific skin concerns and works well on all skin types? This is where the HydraFacial treatment comes into play. HydraFacial treatment is becoming the go-to treatment for anyone wanting to maintain long-term skin health and enhance skin tone and texture. It goes beyond your typical spa treatment to cleanse, extract and hydrate your skin from within.  Sounds amazing, right? But what is a HydraFacial and what does it do to your skin? Our doctors reveal all about this facial treatment and why you should consider it to help you achieve glowing skin.  If you want to discuss HydraFacial treatment in person, you can book an initial consultation at our Leicester clinic.  CONTACT US

But, while the treatment does provide powerful results, it is much more gentle on your skin than your average facial. It is so gentle that we can even use it on sensitive and acne-prone skin types.  In just a single treatment, you will see clearer skin that glows. What are the benefits of getting a HydraFacial?

To help clear clogged pores, we use a gentle solution that contains glycolic and salicylic acid. As this removes dead skin cells and other impurities, it also helps to brighten the skin. This step and step four help make HydraFacial a great acne treatment. 

4.   Extraction

5.   Hydration

After a deep cleanse and extraction, we apply an antioxidant serum. This serum includes a mix of active ingredients, including hyaluronic acid, antioxidants, and peptides. This action gives your skin an instant boost of hydration and helps it look fresh and radiant.  

6.   Rejuvenation

The final step uses LED light therapy to stimulate new collagen in the skin. This is much gentler on the skin than laser treatment and helps to calm redness. 

HydraFacial results – what to expect 

In just one treatment, your skin may look more hydrated and radiant. One treatment is ideal for anyone who wants to rejuvenate their skin before a big event.  If you want to improve a skin condition such as acne scars, fine lines or skin pigmentation, you will need treatments to see great results. We usually recommend a course of 3-4 treatments.  We will also advise you on a skincare routine to follow to help you get the most out of your Hydrafacial treatment. You may also benefit from annual top-up treatments to keep your skin glowing. 

How much does HydraFacial cost?

title: What Is Laser Skin Resurfacing?
author: carteremily
excerpt: If you are dealing with an uneven skin tone, moderate acne scars, or sun-damaged skin, you are likely considering laser skin resurfacing as your ideal solution.
content:
If you are dealing with an uneven skin tone, moderate acne scars, or sun-damaged skin, you are likely considering laser skin resurfacing as your ideal solution. But if you are new to laser treatments, you might be asking yourself what is laser skin resurfacing?  In short, it is a cosmetic procedure that removes the outer, damaged layers of the skin from your face to encourage your body to produce healthy, new skin.  At The One Clinic, our doctors specialise in the use of Erbium YAG laser resurfacing treatment. This is a precise and powerful laser treatment that uses laser light energy to stimulate collagen production, improve skin texture and give you glowing skin.  Read on to hear more from our doctors about laser resurfacing treatment. We will cover more about what this laser treatment is, what it does and how it works.  Or, if you are ready to start your skin transformation, contact our clinic team below to book a personalised consultation, and find out whether laser skin resurfacing is right for you.  CONTACT US

About laser skin resurfacing treatment

If you want to reduce stubborn facial wrinkles, remove acne scars, or even out your skin tone and texture, laser skin resurfacing is one of the best options for achieving optimal results.  Laser resurfacing is also known as a laser peel or laser vaporisation because it uses concentrated beams of laser light energy to remove damaged skin, layer by layer, precisely.   The laser removes the outer layer of the skin (epidermis) and then heats the layers underneath to help promote the growth of new collagen.  The results – you will see skin that looks smoother, firmer and radiant.  We can use laser skin resurfacing treatment to target specific areas of your face, such as wrinkles around your eyes and mouth. Alternatively, you can opt for treatment on your entire face for comprehensive skin rejuvenation.  You can also have laser resurfacing treatment on other areas of the body, such as your hands, neck and décolletage. 

Types of laser skin resurfacing: ablative vs non-ablative lasers

The two main types of laser resurfacing are: ablative lasers and non-ablative laser treatment. 

Non-ablative lasers

Non-ablative treatments are more gentle than ablative lasers.  This is because these devices do not remove the top layers of the skin. Instead, they work by heating the tissue beneath the skin's surface to promote collagen production.  For this reason, non-ablative lasers, such as intense pulsed light (IPL), are better suited for treating mild skin tone issues, hair removal, and active acne.  They do require multiple treatment sessions, more than an ablative laser. 

Ablative lasers

This is a more powerful form of laser resurfacing, as it completely removes the top layer of skin.  For this reason, ablative laser treatment is best suited for those with deep wrinkles, severe or moderate acne scars, and non-responsive skin (where other treatments have not been effective).  Erbium YAG laser resurfacing is a type of ablative laser treatment.  It is one of the best fractional lasers because it delivers laser energy in a more controlled way.  This means we can focus on treating skin conditions such as wrinkles and an uneven skin tone.  Fractional laser resurfacing, including Erbium YAG laser, is similar to carbon dioxide laser (Co2 laser).  However, because it is more precise and causes less heat damage to surrounding tissue, it offers a much shorter recovery period.  It also means that when set to the right parameters, Erbium YAG laser can treat darker skin tones.

How does laser skin resurfacing work?

Consultation

The first step in laser resurfacing treatment is to have a consultation with one of our trained doctors.  They will assess your skin concerns and review your medical history to determine if you are suitable for this treatment.  You will need to have a patch test to ensure your skin type is suitable for treatment.  This is especially true if you have very dark skin.  If you have cold sores or active acne, our doctors will not recommend laser skin resurfacing treatment.  In this instance, they will suggest alternative treatments that will suit your skin type and skin condition. 

The procedure: laser resurfacing

Before you start laser skin resurfacing, your doctor will give you a local anaesthetic to numb the face. This will make the procedure more comfortable for you. If you are only having a small area of your face treated with laser treatment, you may be given a topical numbing cream to numb that area instead.  You will be given an eye shield to protect your eyes from the laser light energy.  During your procedure, the doctor will pass the laser beams over the areas of your face where you have skin issues.  We will use specific laser points and depths to treat various skin concerns and types.  After your erbium laser resurfacing session, your treated skin may appear red and slightly swollen.  This is normal, and you should not be worried.  Your doctor will apply a cream or ointment to the area to help soothe it and support the body's natural healing process.

Laser Skin Resurfacing: How Many Treatments Will I Need?

The number of facial resurfacing sessions you will need depends on the area being treated and your skin issues. For example, acne scars and deep wrinkles may require two to three treatments to achieve the best results.  On average, our patients require 2 to 4 laser skin resurfacing treatments.  We will discuss this with you during your consultation, where you will receive a bespoke treatment plan tailored to your skin type and concerns. 

Book your laser skin resurfacing treatment in Leicester today.

Whether you want to treat deep wrinkles, acne scarring, sun-damaged skin or improve your skin tone, our laser treatment experts at The One Clinic can help.  We use the advanced Erbium YAG laser device to treat all skin types with laser resurfacing treatment. Our doctors can also use it for:
  •       Non-surgical blepharoplasty 
  •       Laser scar treatment
  •       Laser vaginal rejuvenation
  •       Laser for minor surgery, including mole removal

title: Erbium YAG Laser Guide
author: carteremily
excerpt: So, you want to achieve a more youthful glow to your skin without going under the knife or long recovery times.
content:
So, you want to achieve a more youthful glow to your skin without going under the knife or long recovery times? Well, at The One Clinic, we have the answer in the form of Erbium YAG laser skin resurfacing treatment.  This advanced laser treatment is one of the least invasive skin resurfacing options available. It works to target specific skin concerns and improve your overall skin tone and skin texture.  Whether you struggle with acne scarring, dark spots, or sun damage, find out how laser skin resurfacing can help treat these skin conditions with our Erbium YAG laser guide.  If you would prefer to speak to one of our doctors in person, contact our clinic to book a 1-2-1 appointment for Erbium YAG laser treatment.  CONTACT US

What is laser skin resurfacing?

If you want to make a significant improvement to the tone and texture of your skin, then laser skin resurfacing treatment is worth considering. Laser skin resurfacing is a cosmetic procedure that uses concentrated beams of laser light energy to remove the damaged outer layers of the skin. This allows new and healthy skin to grow in its place, which leaves you with a smoother and more radiant complexion.  It is an effective laser treatment to help address and treat various skin disorders. This includes lines and wrinkles, sun-damaged skin and atrophic facial scars (from acne or infection). There are different types of laser skin resurfacing treatments. At The One Clinic, we use the Erbium YAG laser. This is one of the most versatile and precise laser devices on the market. This means great results with less downtime and minimal thermal damage to the skin. 

Introduction to Erbium lasers 

The Erbium YAG laser (also known as Er:YAG laser) is a type of ablative laser, which removes the outer damaged skin layers. It does this by using infrared light to target and remove damaged skin while causing minimal thermal damage to the healthy surrounding skin.  It is one of the most advanced lasers in the range of erbium lasers med sci for treating various skin issues through skin resurfacing. It is one of the most effective laser treatments for tackling and reducing deep wrinkles, acne scars, sun damage and age spots.  Erbium YAG laser uses power and precise laser energy to treat specific areas of the face such as around the eyes or mouth. Equally, it can treat the entire face or different parts of the body, including the hands, neck and décolletage.

Benefits of Erbium YAG laser resurfacing treatment

There are many benefits of having Erbium YAG laser skin resurfacing, including: 
  • The laser device uses a wavelength of 2940nm (laser output) is absorbed by the water in the skin, which means much less heat damage to the skin compared to other lasers such as the CO2 laser.
  • We can customise the laser to treat individual skin concerns and match it to your skin type.
  • It is a non-invasive treatment which means it requires minimal downtime and allows you to return to normal activities much quicker than other lasers. 
  • It is an effective treatment for improving skin tone, skin texture, reducing wrinkles and treating acne scars and sun damage. 
  • Erbium YAG laser also stimulates collagen production in the deep layers of the skin. This helps to promote smoother and firmer skin. 
  • It can be used on darker skin tones by using a specific wavelength. This is why it is considered to be a safer alternative to a carbon dioxide laser for dark skin types. You will still need a patch test first.

How does Erbium YAG laser compare to CO2 lasers for skin resurfacing?

Both the Erbium YAG laser and CO2 lasers are known as ablative laser treatments. This is because they remove the outer layers of the skin.  One of the key differences is that CO2 lasers are more intense, which means that they can treat deeper acne scars and wrinkles. However, because they are more intense, they require a much longer downtime. They also run a higher risk of thermal damage and skin pigmentation issues, which is why they are not suitable for darker skin types.  The Er:YAG laser can help you achieve similar results but without a lot of the side effects you get from CO2 laser treatment. This makes it safer for sensitive skin types and those with darker skin.  The choice between the two laser skin resurfacing treatments will come down to your skin type, the skin issues you want treating and what results you want to achieve.  We know it can be confusing to decide what laser treatment is right for you, which is why we provide every patient with an in-depth consultation. During this appointment, our doctors will develop a tailored treatment plan based on your individual needs and skin goals.  CONTACT US

How the Erbium YAG laser works 

Your doctor will use the erbium YAG laser to emit a laser beam of light energy to target the damaged skin on the surface. This action vaporizes or removes the outer layers of the skin.  The laser treatment works through stimulated emission, which produces a 2940 nm wavelength that is absorbed by the water in your skin.  Our doctors will use specific laser points and depths depending on your skin type and what skin concerns you are wanting to treat.  At the end of your laser resurfacing session, the treatment area will look slightly red and swollen. It can also feel tight and sensitive. This is normal and should only last for a few days. We will provide you with aftercare advice that will help your skin heal and ensure you see great results. 

The results from Erbium YAG laser skin resurfacing treatment

The results you see from laser skin resurfacing will differ from person to person. Most patients will see visible improvements in their skin, including a more even skin tone within two weeks. This happens as the skin heals and any redness and swelling goes down.  Your skin will continue to get better over the next 2-3 months as the new collagen forms. This is when you should see a reduction in wrinkles, less pigmentation and smoother skin. The results from your treatment can last for up to a year. This will depend on your skin needs, skin condition and what skin care routine you follow after treatment.  You may require a top-up treatment once a year to maintain your results and help to prevent future skin issues from appearing.

title: Is Endolift Safe? A Guide on Endolift Side Effects & Safety
author: SumitVirmani
excerpt: Endolift is considered a safe and effective laser treatment when a qualified and experienced practitioner performs it.
content:
Endolift is considered a safe and effective laser treatment when a qualified and experienced practitioner performs it. It uses precise laser energy to tighten the skin and reduce small fat deposits without the need for surgery or general anaesthesia. Most side effects, such as mild swelling or redness, are temporary and part of the normal healing process. If you’re thinking about Endolift but want to understand more about how it works, what to expect, and its possible side effects, this blog is for you. Read till the end to learn what makes it safe, the common and rare side effects of Endolift, and when it's essential to talk to your practitioner after the treatment.

About Endolift Laser Treatment

Endolift is a modern, non-surgical treatment that helps tighten your skin and remove small amounts of fat. It uses a very thin laser fibre, about the width of a hair, which is gently inserted just under the skin. The laser emits energy that warms the tissue and stimulates your body to produce more collagen, keeping your skin firm, smooth, and elastic. Endolift laser skin tightening is safe for the face, jawline, neck, under the chin, and even the arms or tummy. It helps tighten loose skin, reduce fine lines, and create a more sculpted, youthful appearance.

Is Endolift Treatment Safe?

Yes, Endolift is generally considered safe when performed by a trained and qualified practitioner. It’s a minimally invasive procedure that uses precise laser energy to tighten and lift the skin without surgery or general anaesthesia. Here’s why Endolift is considered a safe choice:
  • No Major Cuts or Stitches: The treatment uses a very thin laser fibre, so there’s no need for large incisions. This reduces the risk of scarring or infection.
  • Local Anaesthetic On: A small amount of local anaesthetic keeps you comfortable while avoiding the risks linked with general anaesthesia.
  • Controlled Laser Technology: The laser energy is carefully targeted, ensuring it heats only the needed tissue layers without damaging surrounding skin.
  • FDA-Approved & CE-Marked Equipment: Endolift devices meet strict safety standards, giving patients extra reassurance about their treatment.
  • Quick Recovery: Because it’s non-surgical, most people return to their normal routine within a day or two, with only mild and temporary side effects.
You might experience slight redness, tenderness, or swelling for a short while, but these are normal signs of healing and usually fade within a few days.

Common Endolift Side Effects

After Endolift, most people experience only mild and temporary side effects. These are part of the body’s natural healing process and usually go away within a few days to a week. Common side effects include:

1. Swelling

It’s normal to notice some swelling in the treated area after your procedure. This happens because your skin and tissues are adjusting to the laser treatment. Swelling usually peaks in the first 24–48 hours and starts to go down within a few days.

2. Redness or Warmth

The skin in the treated area may look slightly red or feel warm. This is a normal and expected response to the laser energy and should fade naturally over a few days. Applying cold compresses as advised by your doctor can help ease this.

3. Tenderness or Soreness

You might feel some tenderness or mild soreness where the treatment was done. This is similar to how your skin feels after a gentle bruise and usually disappears in a few days. Over-the-counter pain relief can help if needed.

4. Bruising

Some patients notice minor bruising, especially in areas where the skin is thinner. The bruises are usually light and fade within one to two weeks. Gentle care and following aftercare instructions can speed up healing.

5. Tightness or Numbness

After Endolift, the skin may feel tight or slightly numb for a short period. This is normal and tends to improve on its own within a few days. Massage or gentle movements, if recommended by your practitioner, can help the skin feel more natural again. Even though these side effects are common, they are usually short-lived. Knowing what to expect can help you recover comfortably and get the best results from your Endolift treatment.

Less Common and Rare Side Effects of Endolift

While most side effects of Endolift are mild and short-lived, a few rare effects can occur. Most people do not experience these, but it’s essential to be aware of them.

1. Small Lumps or Irregular Contours

In some cases, small lumps or uneven areas may appear under the skin after treatment. These are usually minor and tend to smooth out on their own as your skin heals. Gentle massage, if recommended by your doctor, can also help the skin feel more even.

2. Temporary Nerve Irritation

A very small number of patients may experience temporary nerve irritation. This can cause a tingling sensation or mild asymmetry around the lips. In most cases, this improves naturally within a few weeks.

3. Skin Burns or Overheating

Burns or overheating of the skin are extremely rare and usually occur only if the laser is used incorrectly. Choosing a trained and experienced practitioner greatly reduces this risk.

4. Infection

Any procedure that involves breaking the skin carries a slight risk of infection. Keeping the treated area clean and following post-treatment advice helps prevent this.

5. Discolouration or Scarring

Persistent skin discolouration or scarring is very uncommon. If it does occur, it is usually mild and can be treated with proper medical care. These rare side effects are uncommon, and most people recover without any long-term problems, but knowing them is essential for you to make informed choices.

Factors That Influence Endolift Safety

Several factors affect how safe your Endolift treatment will be. Understanding these can help you make the best choice and reduce the risk of complications.

1. Practitioner Experience

The skill and experience of your doctor or clinic are the most important factors. A trained professional knows the correct laser settings and technique, which greatly reduces the risk of burns, nerve irritation, or uneven results.

2. Your Health

Your personal health can affect safety. Conditions such as skin infections, autoimmune disorders, or recent cosmetic procedures may make Endolift less suitable. Always share your full medical history with your practitioner.

3. Aftercare Compliance

Following post-treatment instructions is essential. Keeping the area clean, avoiding sun exposure, and limiting strenuous activity helps prevent swelling, bruising, or infection.

4. Equipment and Hygiene

Using proper laser equipment in a clean, controlled environment ensures the procedure is safe and effective. Reputable clinics follow strict hygiene standards to minimise risks. When all these factors are considered, Endolift is a safe and effective treatment for most people.

How Long Does It Take for Endolift Swelling to Go Down?

After Endolift, swelling is a normal part of the healing process. Swelling after Endolift usually resolves within 3 to 7 days, though minor puffiness can persist for up to 2 weeks. This is a normal part of the healing process and does not mean something is wrong. Most swelling peaks within 24 to 48 hours. You may notice mild fullness or puffiness in the treated area, which gradually reduces as your body heals. To help your swelling settle faster:
  • Apply a cold compress in the first 24 hours.
  • Keep your head elevated while resting.
  • Avoid hot baths, saunas, or heavy exercise for a few days.
  • Gentle massage, if your practitioner has recommended it, can also help.
  • With proper care, swelling is temporary and should not affect your final results. Following your doctor’s instructions ensures a smoother and quicker recovery.
Endolift has a high success rate, with most patients seeing noticeable skin tightening and lifting after treatment. Studies and clinical experience show that people are usually satisfied with the results, especially when treated by an experienced practitioner. The success of Endolift also depends on factors like the area being treated, your skin type, and following proper aftercare instructions. Multiple sessions may be recommended in some cases to achieve the best results.

Is an Endolift Worth It?

Yes, Endolift is worth it for many people who want noticeable skin tightening and contouring without surgery. It provides visible results with minimal downtime and fewer risks compared to traditional facelifts. Endolift can improve loose skin, reduce fine lines, and create a more sculpted appearance on areas like the face, jawline, neck, and under the chin. Because it stimulates your body’s own collagen production, the results look natural rather than “pulled” or artificial. It’s especially appealing if you want a non-surgical option with a quick recovery. Most patients can return to their normal activities within a few days while enjoying smoother, firmer skin over the following weeks.

When to Contact Your Practitioner after Endolift

Mild redness, swelling, or tenderness after Endolift is completely normal and usually settles within a few days. However, it’s important to keep an eye on how your skin feels and heals. You should contact your practitioner right away if you notice any of the following:
  • Severe or increasing pain that doesn’t improve with mild pain relief.
  • Swelling or redness that worsens rather than resolves after a few days.
  • Signs of infection, such as warmth, discharge, or fever.
  • Unusual lumps or hard areas under the skin that don’t fade over time.
  • Your practitioner can assess the area and make sure your recovery is on track.
  • Getting professional advice early helps prevent small issues from becoming bigger concerns.

Final Verdict on Endolift Side Effects & Safety

Endolift is a safe and effective option for anyone looking to tighten and lift their skin without surgery. When performed by a qualified practitioner, the procedure has a low risk profile, and most side effects, such as mild swelling, redness, or tenderness, are temporary and settle within a few days. Being aware of potential side effects, following aftercare instructions, and choosing an experienced clinic are the key steps to a smooth recovery and natural-looking results. If you want safe recovery and the best results for you, consult our experts at The Once Clinic for your Endolift treatment. Ultimately, with proper care and guidance, Endolift can deliver noticeable, lasting results while keeping your safety a top priority.

FAQs

1. What is the downtime for Endolift?

Downtime is minimal. Most people can return to normal activities within 1–2 days. Mild swelling, redness, or tenderness may last a few days, but these are normal and temporary.

2. How many times can you do an Endolift?

Endolift can be repeated if needed. Many patients see good results after a single session, but a second treatment may be done after a few months for enhanced tightening or contouring. Your practitioner will recommend the best plan for you.

3. What to avoid after an Endolift?

For the first few days, avoid hot baths, saunas, strenuous exercise, and direct sun exposure. Also, don’t massage or apply strong skincare products to the treated area unless your practitioner advises it.

4. How to heal faster after an Endolift?

Follow your practitioner’s aftercare instructions carefully. Keeping the area clean, using cold compresses in the first 24 hours, staying hydrated, and avoiding heavy activity help the skin recover faster and reduce swelling or bruising.

5. What is the best age for an Endolift?

Endolift is suitable for adults who have mild to moderate skin laxity or early signs of ageing. Many patients are in their 30s to 50s, but it can be effective for older adults too, depending on skin condition and goals. Your practitioner can advise if it’s right for you.

title: How Long Does Endolift Last? All About Endolift Results

content:
Endolift stand out in how real the results look. There’s no “pulled” or “overdone” look, just smoother, firmer skin that still feels like you.  If you’re curious how it works, when you’ll see changes, and what helps those results last even longer, let’s take a closer look.

What Is Endolift?

Endolift is a modern laser treatment that helps tighten the skin and shape the face without surgery. It works by using a very fine laser fibre that goes just under the skin through a tiny opening. The laser gently warms the deeper layers, which makes the skin tighten and start producing new collagen. Collagen is what keeps our skin firm, smooth, and youthful.  As we age, we naturally lose some of it, and that’s when skin starts to sag. Endolift helps your body produce more collagen, giving your skin a lifted, fresher look. Explore the complete Endolift guide to learn its ins and outs.

When Will You See Endolift Results?

You can see some Endolift results straight after treatment, but the full effect develops over the next few months. Most people notice their skin becoming firmer and smoother within 3 to 6 months as new collagen forms and tightens the skin. Straight after your session, you might see a slight lift or feel your skin tighten. This happens because the laser gently warms the tissue, making it contract. Over time, your body builds new collagen, which improves firmness and smoothness from within. Your results continue to improve naturally, reaching their best around the six-month mark and can stay visible for years with good care. Endolift gives gradual, natural-looking changes, so your skin looks fresher, not “done.” Is Endolift safe? Yes, Endolift is a safe skin-tightening laser treatment when performed by a professional.

How Long Do Endolift Results Last?

Endolift results usually last 2 to 3 years, and in some people, up to 5 years. The exact time varies from person to person, depending on things like age, lifestyle, and skin condition. Right after treatment: You’ll notice some firmness, but your results keep improving for months as your skin makes new collagen. This new collagen helps the skin stay lifted and smooth long after your session. Over time, your body’s natural ageing process continues, but you can help your results last longer with healthy habits and good skincare. Many people choose to have a small top-up treatment after about a year to keep their skin looking its best.

What Affects How Long Endolift Lasts?

Everyone’s skin is different, so Endolift results don’t last the same for everyone. How long your results stay depends on a few key things:

  • Age

Younger skin makes collagen more easily, so results often last longer. Older skin can still respond well, but the collagen may build a little more slowly.

  • Lifestyle

Healthy habits help your skin stay firm and smooth. Too much sun, smoking, stress, or lack of sleep can make collagen break down faster. Eating well, drinking enough water, and getting rest all help your results last longer.

  • Skincare Routine

Using gentle products that protect and feed your skin makes a big difference. A daily SPF, plus creams with vitamin C or hyaluronic acid, can help keep your skin firm.

  • Treatment Area

Some areas, like the face or neck, move more and may lose tightness sooner than places that move less. Keeping a steady weight also helps if your Endolift was for fat reduction, like under the chin.

  • Number of Endolift Sessions

Most people need only one Endolift session. But having a touch-up after 12 to 18 months can refresh and extend your results. All these small things add up. Taking care of your skin and health helps your Endolift results last as long as possible.

How to Keep Your Endolift Results Last Longer

You can help your Endolift results last much longer by looking after your skin and body. Small, simple steps make a big difference. Here are some easy ways to keep your skin firm and glowing for years:

  • Protect Your Skin from the Sun

Sunlight breaks down collagen and can make your skin age faster. Apply sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher every day, even when it’s cloudy or cold.

  • Stay Healthy Inside and Out

A diet full of fruit, vegetables, and lean protein helps your skin stay healthy and heal well after the treatment. Drink plenty of water to keep yourself hydrated and fresh.

  • Keep a Good Skincare Routine

Use gentle, high-quality products that suit your skin type. Look for ingredients like vitamin C, retinol, or hyaluronic acid to support collagen and keep skin smooth.

  • Avoid Smoking and Limit Alcohol

Smoking and too much alcohol can damage collagen and make results fade sooner. Staying smoke-free helps your skin stay firm for longer.

  • Book Maintenance Treatments on Time

Some people like to have a small top-up session every year or two to refresh results and boost collagen again. Your skin specialist can guide you on the best plan for you. With a little care, your Endolift results can stay fresh and natural for many years.

Who Gets the Best Endolift Results?

Endolift can work well for many people, but some see longer-lasting results than others. Your skin’s age, condition, and lifestyle all play a part in how well your body responds. People who often get the best results are those who:
  • Have mild to moderate skin sagging rather than very loose skin.
  • Are in good overall health and keep a stable weight.
  • Protect their skin from the sun and follow a gentle skincare routine.
  • Don’t smoke and eat a balanced diet rich in vitamins and water.
  • Be patient, knowing that results take time to develop fully.
You don’t have to be young to enjoy the benefits. Endolift helps people of all ages look fresher and more lifted. However, keeping up healthy habits and looking after your skin can help your results last longer and look even better over time.

Endolift Maintenance Treatments

Like any skin treatment, Endolift works best when you give your skin a little care over time. The results can last for years, but a small maintenance session can help keep your skin firm and glowing for even longer. Many people choose to have a top-up treatment after about 12 to 18 months. This refreshes the collagen under the skin and helps to hold the lift you already have. Each time you do it, your skin becomes a little stronger and more supported. Your skin specialist will check how your results are lasting and can suggest the best time for your next treatment. Regular reviews help make sure you keep your natural, youthful look without ever needing surgery. Remember: Endolift maintenance is quick and gentle and helps you stay one step ahead of ageing.

Capping it all on Endolift Results & Their Longevity

Endolift is more than a quick fix; it’s a smart way to refresh your skin from within. The results can last for 2-3 years or more (in some cases), and with a bit of care, your skin can stay firm, lifted, and glowing well into the future. Everyone’s results are slightly different, but the beauty of Endolift is that it works with your body’s natural collagen to bring out your best, most confident self. Our experts are here to guide you every step of the way, from your first chat to your final results. Most people only need one Endolift session to see great results. A small top-up after 6–12 months can help maintain and refresh the lift.

2. What are the disadvantages of Endolift?

You might notice some swelling or bruising for up to 2 weeks after treatment. Rarely, temporary side effects such as mild skin burns or colour changes can occur, but these usually settle with time.

Yes, for many people, Endolift is worth it. It tightens skin, boosts collagen, and naturally shapes the face, all without surgery or extended downtime. The results look subtle, last for years, and the treatment is more affordable than a facelift.

4. How many years does an Endolift last?

Endolift is best for people aged 30 to 60 with mild to moderate skin sagging. But age isn’t everything; your skin’s condition matters more than your number of birthdays.

title: How Much Does Endolift Cost?
author: carteremily
excerpt: Endolift has become a popular choice for people who want tighter skin and better facial contour without surgery.
content:
Endolift has become a popular choice for people who want tighter skin and better facial contour without surgery. It uses special laser fibres that work under the skin to tighten tissue and melt small pockets of fat. Many people choose it because it gives visible improvement with very little downtime. If you are thinking about getting Endolift, one of the first questions you will have is the cost. This guide explains everything you need to know about Endolift pricing. You will learn how much it usually costs, what factors change the price, what you should ask during a consultation, and how Endolift compares with other treatments.

What is Endolift, and Why Can the Cost Vary?

Endolift is a minimally invasive laser treatment. A very thin fibre is inserted under the skin. The laser heats the tissue, causing it to contract and resulting in firmer skin and a more defined shape. It can also reduce small fat areas like the double chin or jowls. The results often look natural because the treatment works with your body's own collagen. Endolift costs more than simple surface laser treatments because:
  • The equipment is advanced.
  • The procedure requires trained and skilled practitioners.
  • The technique takes precision and planning.
  • High-quality disposable fibres are used for each session.
Since it works under the skin, the treatment is more technical than a standard laser or radiofrequency session. That added complexity is part of what you pay for.

Endolift Cost by Areas in the UK

If you want a quick idea of Endolift prices in the UK, here are the most common ranges based on typical clinic rates. These numbers help you understand what to expect before you book a consultation.

1. Single Focused Area

Starting from around £1,500 This includes smaller zones such as the jawline, under the chin, or the under-eye area. These areas take less time and require fewer laser fibres. The cost stays on the lower side because the treatment zone is compact and the procedure is usually faster.

2. Full Face

Around £2,950 Full face treatment covers cheeks, jawline, smile lines and the lower facial area. This option gives balanced tightening and contouring across the entire face. It is a popular choice for people who want an overall lifted look instead of treating one area at a time.

3. Full Face and Neck

Approximately £3,500 This is one of the most requested combinations because the neck and face age together. Treating both at once creates a smooth transition and a more natural result. The neck requires more time and careful technique, which increases the total price.

4. Abdomen or Waist

Around £2,500 Endolift can also be used on body areas to tighten loose skin and reduce small fat pockets. The abdomen or waist area is larger than the face, so the session takes longer and uses more energy. This is why the cost falls in the mid to higher range.

What Affects the Cost of Endolift?

Many factors influence the price of an Endolift treatment, and understanding them helps you know why costs vary.

1. Treatment area and size

The bigger the area, the higher the cost. Treating a small area, like under the chin, costs less than a full face and neck treatment. Larger areas take more time, more fibres, and more laser energy.

2. Experience of the provider

Doctors with strong experience in cosmetic laser procedures usually charge more. This is normal because skill plays a large role in how safe and effective your result will be. An experienced provider knows how deep the fibre should go, how much energy to use, and how to shape the treated zone for a natural look.

3. Location of the clinic

Clinics in major cities usually charge more. Cities have higher operating costs and often attract top specialists, which raises prices. On the other hand, medical tourism destinations may offer lower prices, but you should also consider travel costs, accommodation, and follow-up care.

4. Number of sessions

Most people see good results from one session, but some need more, depending on skin condition. Some clinics sell single sessions. Others offer packages. A package may include follow-ups or small touch-ups for a better overall result.

5. Extra treatments combined with Endolift

Many clinics combine Endolift with other treatments such as fillers, thread lifts, or skin resurfacing. This improves results but increases total cost. If you want a natural lift and a smoother surface at the same time, your price may reflect the combined plan.

6. Precare and aftercare

Some clinics include numbing injections, consultation, checkups, medication, and follow-up visits in the total price. Always ask what is included so you are not surprised later.

Is Endolift worth the cost?

To understand value, compare it with other options.

Compared with a surgical facelift

A facelift gives a much stronger lift but involves surgery, higher cost, longer downtime, and anaesthesia. Endolift is less intense and works well for moderate sagging. If you want a natural improvement without surgery, Endolift can offer good value.

Compared with ultrasound or radiofrequency

Ultrasound and radiofrequency treatments are fully noninvasive and usually cost less. The downside is many require multiple sessions, and they may not reshape small fat pockets the way Endolift does. Endolift combines tightening and contouring in one treatment.

Compared with thread lifts or fillers

Threads and fillers can give quick results and cost less at first. Fillers add volume, threads give some lift, and both may need regular maintenance. Endolift focuses on tightening and long-term improvement in collagen. In many cases, clinics combine these treatments for balanced results. The best choice depends on your goals. Some people need a blend of treatments to get the result they want.

Questions To Ask Before Booking

Ask these during your consultation to protect yourself and avoid surprises:
  • What is included in the price?
  • Is this the final price, or will I need to pay extra for anaesthesia, medications, or follow-up?
  • How many Endolift procedures have you performed?
  • Can you show me before and after photos of your own patients?
  • What kind of results can I expect, and how long will they last?
  • What happens if I am not satisfied with the result?
  • How do you handle complications?
  • How many days of recovery should I plan for?
  • For medical tourism: how will you support me once I return home?

How To Decide If Endolift Is Right For You?

Step 1. Know your main goal

Do you want mild tightening, reduction of a double chin, improved jawline, or help with early sagging. Endolift is ideal for mild to moderate concerns.

Step 2. Choose the right provider

A skilled practitioner can make the difference between a small improvement and a great result. Choose someone trained and experienced in Endolift specifically.

Step 3. Compare detailed quotes

Check what is included. Some clinics offer a low price but charge extra for consultations, medications, or aftercare.

Step 4. Think about long-term value

If one Endolift session gives results that last one to three years, the cost per year may be better than repeated smaller treatments.

Step 5. Consider safety and follow-up

Choose a clinic with strong medical standards. Good aftercare support is important even for minimally invasive treatments.

Considering Endolift at The One Clinic?

If you are exploring Endolift and want expert guidance, The One Clinic focuses on personalised consultations rather than fixed, one-size-fits-all pricing. Every face and skin type is different, so a detailed assessment helps determine whether Endolift is suitable for your concerns and what level of improvement you can realistically expect. At The One Clinic, a qualified specialist will evaluate your skin laxity, facial structure, and goals before recommending a tailored treatment plan. This ensures the procedure is safe, effective, and aligned with natural-looking results rather than over-treatment.

Final Thoughts

Endolift offers a good balance between results and minimal downtime. Although it costs more than simple noninvasive treatments, it provides a deeper level of tightening and contouring without surgery. Most people can expect to pay between £1,500 and £5,000. Prices depend on the area treated, the provider's skill, the clinic's location, and whether the treatment includes additional services. The key is to choose your clinic based on quality, not just cost. A proper consultation, clear communication, and full price transparency will help you make the best decision for your goals.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Is an Endolift worth it?

Endolift is a good choice for people who have mild or moderate sagging and want results without surgery. It can tighten skin, shape the face, and reduce small fat pockets with little downtime. It is not meant to replace a facelift for heavy sagging, so a consultation is important to know if it fits your needs.

2. How long does the Endolift last?

Most people enjoy results for about two to three years. Some may notice effects lasting a bit less or more, depending on age, skin quality, and lifestyle. The improvement continues for months as new collagen forms, and many patients choose a light touch-up after a year or two.

3. How painful is an Endolift?

Endolift is usually easy to tolerate. The doctor numbs the area with a local anaesthetic so you stay comfortable. You may feel slight warmth or pressure, but most people report only mild discomfort.

4. What to avoid after an Endolift?

Skip heavy workouts for the first 48 hours to reduce swelling. Also, stay away from saunas, steam rooms, and sunbeds for about a week or until the skin settles.

5. How many times can you do an Endolift?

Most people need only one session. Some choose a second session within a year if they have more laxity or want stronger improvement. Touch-ups every couple of years can help maintain the lift as you age.

title: Endolift Aftercare: A Guide To Amazing Results
author: carteremily
excerpt: Endolift aftercare focuses on helping your skin heal safely and achieve the best results after treatment.
content:
Endolift aftercare focuses on helping your skin heal safely and achieve the best results after treatment. In the first few days, it’s essential to rest your skin, wear a compression strap, apply ice compressions, avoid excessive heat, and follow your practitioner’s guidance closely. Staying gentle with your skincare and protecting your skin from the sun make a big difference in how well you recover. If you’ve just had an Endolift or are planning one soon, this blog is for you. Here, we’ll guide you through every stage of the aftercare process, from the first 24 hours to long-term care, so you know exactly how to support your skin after treatment.

What Is Endolift Aftercare?

After your Endolift treatment, proper care is crucial to help your skin heal and achieve optimal results. Below, we’ve broken down the aftercare step by step, from the first hours after treatment to long-term care, so that you can support your skin safely and effectively.

Endolift Aftercare Timeline: Step-by-Step Recovery Guide

First 24-48 Hours: Protect & Soothe

Your first day or two after Endolift are crucial for proper healing. These initial hours set the tone for your recovery.

1. Avoid Touching or Rubbing the Treated Area

Your skin is delicate immediately after the Endolift procedure. Touching or rubbing the area can slow down healing and may cause unnecessary irritation. Keep your hands away from your face as much as possible.

2. Keep Your Head Elevated While Sleeping

Sleeping with your head slightly raised helps reduce swelling. Using an extra pillow or a wedge pillow can make a big difference in how quickly your face settles. This simple step supports a smoother recovery.

3. Apply Cold Compresses Daily

For 10-15 minutes every few hours, apply cold compressions. It can help soothe discomfort and reduce swelling, making your skin feel calmer. Avoid using the ice directly on the skin; wrap it in a soft cloth to prevent direct contact.

4. Avoid Heat & Do Not Apply Makeup

Avoid wearing makeup for at least the first day, and do not go to the saunas, steam rooms, or very hot showers. Heat can increase blood flow to your skin and worsen swelling or redness. Let your skin breathe during these initial hours.

5. Stay Hydrated

Drinking plenty of water helps your body flush out toxins and supports healing. Hydration also keeps your skin supple, which can improve your Endolift results. Aim for at least 1.5-2 litres of water each day.

Days 3-7: Reduce Swelling & Support Healing

These first few days continue the healing process. Proper care now helps prevent swelling and supports the lift.

1. Wear Your Compression Strap or Garment

Following your provider’s advice on compression is essential. Typically, you wear it full-time for the first three days and overnight until day 10. This helps your skin settle and supports the lifting effect.

2. Avoid Strenuous Exercise

Heavy exercise can increase blood flow and swelling in the treated area. Stick to gentle walks or light activity, and avoid workouts that cause you to sweat heavily until your healthcare provider says it’s safe.

3. Apply Soothing Creams

Using gentle creams like Avène Cicalfate or Arnica Gel can help calm redness and irritation. Always check with your provider which products are safe, as harsh ingredients may slow down recovery.

4. Use Gentle Cleansers and Moisturisers

Stick to fragrance-free, soft skincare products. Avoid harsh soaps or exfoliants, which can irritate your skin. Simple cleansing and moisturising will keep your skin protected while it heals.

5. Adjust Your Sleeping Routine

Once swelling reduces, you can start sleeping without the strap during the day. Maintaining a slightly elevated head at night can still help keep swelling down, but you don’t need the strap 24/7 anymore.

Weeks 2-4: Gentle Recovery and Skin Boost

By week two, most initial swelling has settled. You can start reintroducing normal activities carefully.

1. Resume Light Daily Activities

By week two, most swelling and redness will have reduced. You can start normal daily routines, but check with your provider before returning to intense exercise. Slow reintroduction prevents over-stressing the treated area.

2. Stick To Your Sun Protection (SPF)

Your skin is still sensitive, so protecting it from the sun's rays is essential. Use SPF 50+ and avoid prolonged direct sun exposure to prevent pigmentation and irritation.

3. Start Gentle Lymphatic Drainage Massage

If your practitioner allows, gently massage your skin at night for about 15 minutes, focusing on the area under your chin and neck. Massage may minimise remaining swelling, improve circulation, and support final contouring.

4. Maintain Hydration and a Healthy Diet

Keep drinking water and eating a balanced diet rich in protein and vitamin C. These nutrients support collagen formation and overall skin recovery.

5. Avoid Harsh Skincare

Do not use chemical peels, strong exfoliants, or facials during this period. Your skin is still in recovery mode and needs gentle care to prevent irritation or setbacks.

Long-Term Care (Month 2 and Beyond)

Even after your skin feels normal, proper care ensures your results last. Long-term attention keeps your skin looking its best.”

1. Keep Using Sunscreen Daily

Even after your skin feels normal, continue using SPF daily. Long-term sun protection helps prevent pigmentation and maintains the lifting effect of Endolift.

2. Reintroduce Active Skincare Slowly

You can gradually start using products like vitamin C serums or retinol creams, but introduce them one at a time. This helps your skin adjust and avoids unnecessary irritation.

3. Attend Follow-Up Appointments

Check in with your provider to monitor your recovery and see the final results. They can also guide you on any additional treatments or touch-ups that may be needed.

4. Consider Yearly Maintenance Treatments

Some patients benefit from yearly follow-up treatments to maintain results. Discuss this with your clinic to decide what is best for your skin and lifestyle.

Why Taking Care After Endolift Treatment Matters?

Endolift aftercare is just as important as the treatment itself. Proper care helps your skin heal faster, reduces swelling, and prevents side effects like bruising or irritation. Proper aftercare allows the collagen-boosting effects to work their best for long-lasting firmness and lift, which ultimately makes your results amazing. Skipping aftercare can slow down recovery and affect the evenness and smoothness of your final results.

What To Avoid After Endolift (and Why)?

Certain activities or habits can slow healing, increase swelling, or affect your final results. Here’s a clear guide on what to steer clear of and why.

1. Avoid Strenuous Exercise

Intense workouts increase blood flow and can worsen swelling in the treated areas. Prefer gentle movement, like walking, during the first week or until your provider says it’s safe. This helps your skin heal smoothly without unnecessary pressure.

2. Stay Away from Heat

Hot showers, saunas, steam rooms, or sunbathing can make swelling worse and irritate healing skin. For at least the first week to ensure your skin recovers properly, you must avoid them all. Keeping your skin cool helps your results settle evenly.

3. Do Not Touch or Massage Too Early

Your skin is delicate right after Endolift. Rubbing, pressing, or massaging the treated areas too soon can disrupt healing tissue and affect the lift. Wait for your provider’s guidance before starting any massage.

4. Avoid Harsh Skincare Products

Chemical exfoliants, retinol, or strong acids can irritate the skin during recovery. Stick to gentle cleansers and moisturisers recommended by your provider until your skin has fully healed. This prevents redness or delayed recovery.

5. Limit Alcohol and Smoking

Both alcohol and smoking can affect blood circulation and slow the healing process. Cutting back or avoiding them during recovery will help your skin repair faster and support long-lasting results.

Signs to Watch Out For During Endolift Aftercare

While most people heal smoothly after Endolift, it’s essential to know when something isn’t right. Warning signs include:
  • Pain that is getting severe.
  • Swelling that suddenly increases or doesn’t improve.
  • Persistent redness or heat in the treated area.
  • Any unusual fluid, pus, or signs of infection.
  • Prolonged numbness or muscle weakness.
Contact your provider immediately if you notice any of the signs mentioned above.

Additional Endolift Aftercare: Expert Tips for Smooth Recovery 

A few small habits can make a big difference to how well your skin heals after Endolift. Follow these tips to stay comfortable and enjoy smoother, faster results.

1. Eat Skin-Healing Foods

Include foods rich in protein, vitamin C, and antioxidants. They help your skin build new collagen and accelerate recovery after treatment.

2. Stay Hydrated

Drink plenty of water throughout the day. Hydration helps flush toxins from your body and keeps your skin fresh and supple.

3. Get Enough Sleep

Aim for at least 7–8 hours of sleep each night. Rest allows your skin to repair naturally and supports a glowing, healthy look.

4. Avoid Taking Flights In The Early Days

For the first 48 hours after treatment, try not to fly, because cabin pressure may worsen swelling and slow down healing.

5. Track Your Results

Take photos weekly or monthly to see how your skin changes over time. It’s a great way to notice gradual tightening and stay motivated.

Final Verdict

For endolift aftercare, keep your head slightly raised, wear your compression garment as advised, avoid heat or makeup for a few days, and take rest. These small steps make a big difference in how smoothly your skin heals and how natural your results look. If you’re considering a facelift without surgery, consider Endolift. Our specialists can guide you through the process and tailor the treatment to your skin’s needs. Book a consultation today and take the first step towards firmer, more defined skin.

FAQs

1. How long are you swollen after Endolift?

Swelling after Endolift usually lasts between 2 and 14 days. It often peaks around days 5 or 6 and then slowly fades. Most people feel comfortable returning to social life within two weeks. Mild redness may fade sooner, often within the first 48 hours. Keeping your head elevated, using cold compresses, and following your provider’s aftercare advice can help swelling go down faster.

2. Should I wear a compression garment after an Endolift?

Yes. Wearing a compression strap or garment after Endolift helps your skin settle smoothly and supports healing. It gently holds the treated area in place, reducing swelling and helping the skin tighten properly.

3. What is the downtime for Endolift?

Endolift has very little downtime. You can usually return to light daily activities within a day or two, although mild swelling or redness may last for a few days. Most people feel fully comfortable within a week.

4. Will elevating my head reduce swelling?

Yes. Keeping your head raised while resting or sleeping helps reduce swelling. It prevents fluid from gathering in the treated area and allows your skin to settle faster. Using an extra pillow or a wedge under your head is an easy way to prevent swelling.

5. How can I speed up healing after the laser on my face?

To help your skin heal faster, stay hydrated and use gentle moisturisers as recommended by your provider. Apply SPF and skip harsh products or treatments until your skin has fully recovered. A calm, clean, and moisturised routine works best.
